findings.title: HVAC spend in 2026-06 was +72% against its own baseline
findings.description: $1,810 in 2026-06 versus a baseline mean of $1,050. No single entry dominates the month.
findings.recommendation: Verify invoice scope and coding. Treat the variance as explained only after confirming whether this was one-time work, recurring work, or a miscoded charge.

findings.title: Acme HVAC accounts for 88.3% of HVAC spend
findings.description: $7,960 of $9,010 total hvac spend across 2 vendors in this file. Concentration is a dependency signal, not evidence of bad pricing or misconduct.
findings.recommendation: Compare scope, response time, pricing and backup-vendor capacity before changing procurement.

findings.title: 1 exact duplicate group(s) found, extra-row face value $650
findings.description: Each group shares an identical date, vendor, category and amount. The ledger has no invoice number or work-order ID, so even an exact match is only a candidate until source documents are checked.
findings.recommendation: Match each group to invoice number, work order, unit/location and proof of service before requesting any credit.

findings.title: 1 same-vendor, same-amount charge pair(s) within 7 days on different dates
findings.description: Acme HVAC: $900 on 2026-07-16 and 2026-07-19. Same amount on nearby dates is not enough to call this duplicate billing -- split invoices, staged work and recurring service all look identical here.
findings.recommendation: Compare invoice and job identifiers. Keep this separate from exact-duplicate counts unless the supporting documents match.

findings.title: 1 credit/reversal line(s) totalling -$180
findings.description: Spread across 1 category. Credits offset spend in the same category, which can make a monthly baseline non-positive and its variance unreportable.
findings.recommendation: Confirm each credit is matched to the original charge, and that the offset landed in the period you expect.

findings.title: 2 open item(s) older than 30 days, totalling $1,180
findings.description: 1 are older than 90 days, totalling $420. They span 2 different categories, so this file does not support a claim that aging is concentrated in any one of them. Age is measured to 2026-08-01.
findings.recommendation: Confirm what 'open' means in the source system -- unpaid, unresolved, awaiting approval or uncleared -- before assigning an operational cause.

window.baselineFormula: Arithmetic mean of monthly category spend, 2026-01 through 2026-05 (5 month(s))
